title: Trace Preservation Gateway: SDK middleware for cross-process request fidelity
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Implement a lightweight Trace Preservation Gateway (TPG) as an SDK middleware and optional edge-side proxy to ensure high-fidelity propagation of request provenance and sampling hints across heterogeneous clients and internal services. TPG will focus on: 1) canonicalizing incoming trace metadata (multi-format headers), 2) preserving sampling decision and application-level attributes across async boundaries, and 3) emitting compact, deterministic breadcrumbs that downstream collectors can stitch without expensive de-dup logic. The goal is to reduce missing-span and orphaned-span cases observed in multi-protocol flows and improve trace completeness for tail-latency incidents.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware implemented for JS/Go/Java with a uniform API for attach/detach of request context
Header canonicalizer supports x-request-id, traceparent, b3, and our internal provenance envelope and normalizes them into a single carrier
End-to-end integration test demonstrating propagation across HTTP -> async queue -> worker with <0.5ms middleware overhead on p50 path
Dashboard metric: trace_linkage_rate increased by 8% on a synthetic multi-hop workload; missing-span rate decreased by 30% in canary services
Documentation and migration guide published (Confluence link) and one staged canary rollout completed without increased error budgets
design_decisions: Use a pull-style carrier model in SDKs to avoid duplicate copies of large baggage and to limit heap retention in server runtimes

Canonicalizer will translate legacy B3 and Traceparent headers into an internal 'rwd-prov' header with base64-encoded compact provenance; full headers kept in logs for debugging but not sent downstream by default
Provide an opt-in edge-side proxy component (Go) for customers that cannot upgrade SDKs, with conservatively parsimonious behavior to avoid header amplification
Default sampling hints are preserved as immutable once set at gateway ingress to avoid sampling flip-flop across retries/queues
tradeoffs: Compact provenance reduces wire size but requires deterministic serializers; may hinder some debuggability without explicit 'debug' mode
Pull-style carrier reduces allocation but adds a small callsites cost in hot paths — mitigated by inlining-friendly APIs and JIT hints for JS
Edge proxy covers unupgraded clients but increases operational surface (config/ops) — prefer SDK-first adoption for performance-sensitive teams
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): ship JS SDK middleware and proxy, enable on 2 internal services; run for 72h and validate trace_linkage_rate
Phase 2 (expand): ship Go and Java SDKs, enable automatic header canonicalization on ingress LB for non-library traffic
Phase 3 (broad): opt-in rollout to selected customers via feature flag; provide migration guide and toggle for proxy fallback
Rollback criteria: >1% increase in 5xx or 50ms regression in p95 application latency after middleware enabled
testing_plan: Unit tests for the canonicalizer matrix (b3, traceparent, x-request-id combos)
Integration test harness using synthetic multi-hop pipeline (HTTP -> Kafka-like queue -> worker) validating trace stitching
Performance microbenchmarks with and without middleware across JS/Go/Java to ensure overhead targets
Fuzz tests for malformed header inputs and large baggage scenarios to ensure graceful degradation
monitoring: trace_linkage_rate (service-level): fraction of traces with >1 linked spans across hops
missing_span_rate: fraction of spans expected but absent in stitched traces
middleware_tail_latency_ms: p50/p95 cost added by middleware per language
canonicalization_errors: count of headers we could not parse or normalized with warnings
canary_alert: auto abort rollout if missing_span_rate increases after enablement
